To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) SR involves the top down and bottom-up regulation of action, emotion and cognition; (b) the top-down aspects of SR involve cognitive control and EF; (c) the bottom-up aspects of SR are represented by EC; (d) the breakdowns of SR in psychopathology include impulsive, risky, and disinhibited behaviors; and (e) SR can be organized hierarachically in relation to its granularity, developmental time course, and developmental trajectory.
the field needs a general construct of SR and that it is important for the field to integrate the various aspects of top down SR.
the field needs a more integrated approach to SR, and that SR can be organized hierarcically in relation to development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of individual differences in self regulation (SR) and how they relate to psychopathology.
the development of self regulation, or the ability to exert control over one's own behavior, thoughts and emotions.
how children learn to control their thoughts, feelings, and actions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self regulation is the process of exerting control over one's own thoughts, feelings, and actions.

SR is the domain general construct of interest, but that the specific aspects of SR that are relevant to a given developmental psychopathology will be determined by the specific aspects of the disorder.

self regulation is a complex and multi-level phenomenon, and that the various levels of SR are related to each other, but not in a simple way, and are related to various aspects of developmental psychopathology in a complex and nuanced way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SR is a domain general construct encompassing top down and bottom-up aspects of regulation of emotion, cognition, and behavior, and that it includes basic processes that develop earlier and address immediate conflicts (cognitive control, EC, and related constructs), and complex processes that develop later and address future conflicts (complex aspects of executive function).
self regulation is an umbrella term for a variety of processes that are involved in the control of thoughts, feelings, and actions.
SR is a domain general, multifaceted construct that includes both top down and basic processes, and that it can be hierarchically organized.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the field needs to move away from the current situation in which there are many terms that are used interchangeably and that refer to the same constructs, and instead move toward a more precise terminology and a more precise conceptualization of the SR construct.

the field needs to move away from a focus on a single process and instead consider a more comprehensive view of SR that encompasses multiple components, and that the hierarchical view is useful for integrating across these multiple components.
the SR universe is a complex one, with multiple aspects that are distinct and related in different ways.
